What is a free stuff website?

A free stuff website is one page that collects real free offers from real brands, so you do not have to hunt for them one by one. This page lists 63 offers, all taken from the brands' own official sites. There are three kinds here. Free trials let you try a paid app free for 7 to 30 days — for example Word, YouTube Premium or Apple TV+. Free-forever plans cost nothing at all, for as long as you use them. And discounts cut the price of software, games, courses and hosting, sometimes by 70 to 90 percent. Everything here is for everyone. You do not need a student ID, a special email or an invitation — if the offer says “Global”, anyone in most countries can claim it. Some offers ask for a card to start a trial; those are marked “Card needed”, and every trial card on this page tells you how long the trial lasts and what it costs after, so you can cancel before you are charged. Claiming an offer is simple: open it, tap the button, and sign up on the brand's own official website. Prices and trial lengths can change, and they can differ by country, so always check the official site before you pay.

Global digital offers only — no US-only mailed samples. Every offer here is something you can use online: an app, a piece of software, a streaming service, a course or a game. You will not find mailed samples, food coupons or furniture giveaways here — those only work in one country, and this list is for everyone, everywhere.

Who checks these offers: every offer is checked against the brand's own official site only, and the whole list is reviewed every week.

How to spot a fake free offer

Most "free" traps follow the same pattern. Check these four things before you sign up for anything:

  • Check the official site first. A real free offer lives on the brand's own website. If a link, ad or message sends you somewhere else, stop.
  • Never give a card number or ID number for a "free" sample. A real free sample never asks for your card number, bank details or an ID number like an SSN. If it asks, it is not free — it is a trap.
  • If it sounds impossible, it is. A free phone for $1, or a $500 gift card for one click, is never real.
  • Read the trial end date before you sign up. Note the date, set a reminder a few days before, and cancel from the brand's own site or app if you do not want to pay.

How every offer is checked

  • Official site only. Every offer is read on the brand's own website — never copied from a blog, a coupon site or a social post.
  • Card status is marked. If an offer needs a card to start, its card says “Card needed” before you click anything.
  • Trial terms are shown. Every free trial shows its length and the price after it ends, on the card itself.
  • Re-checked every week. The whole list is checked again each week. Offers that stop working come off the list, and the check date at the top of this page is updated.

Frequently asked questions

Are these really free?

Yes — every offer on this page comes from the brand's own official site. "Free forever" offers cost nothing at all. Free trials cost nothing during the trial, but they turn into a paid plan if you do not cancel — and every trial card shows the price after the trial, so you know before you start.

Do I need a card?

Some offers, yes. The free trials — 18 of the 63 offers — ask for a card to start and are marked "Card needed". The free-forever plans ask only for an email to sign up.

Is this site free to use?

Yes. Looking at this page and using it costs nothing — no account, no sign-up and no payment. The buttons take you straight to each brand's official site, and this page never asks for your card or bank details.

How long do free trials last?

The trials on this page run from 7 days to 1 month. Apple TV+ and Skillshare give 7 days; Microsoft 365 and Amazon Prime give a full month. Every trial card shows its length and the price after the trial ends, so check that line before you sign up.

What happens if I forget to cancel?

The trial turns into a paid subscription and your card is charged. Set a reminder on the day you sign up, a few days before the trial ends, and cancel from the brand's own site or app.

Why do companies give things away for free?

It is marketing. A free plan or a free trial lets you try the real product, and the company hopes you will like it enough to stay or pay later. A few offers are free by design: Khan Academy and freeCodeCamp are non-profits, so their lessons cost nothing for anyone. Nothing on this page is a prize draw — every offer is open to everyone who signs up.

What information is safe to give when I claim an offer?

On the brand's own official site, your name and email address are normal, and a card is normal for a free trial. Never give a bank login or an ID number like an SSN, and never give a card number for a free sample — a real sample never asks for one. If a page asks for any of those, close it.

Do offers work worldwide?

These are global digital offers — apps, software, streaming, courses and games you use online. A few offers vary by country: the trial length or the price can differ, and a small number may not be available everywhere. The official site shows what applies in your country.

Which offers can I claim without a card?

The free-forever plans — 45 of the 63 offers — ask only for an email to sign up. Good first claims: Epic Games Store (a free PC game every week), ChatGPT, Canva, Spotify's free plan, Khan Academy and Google Drive's 15 GB of free storage.

How do you check offers?

Every offer is checked against the brand's own official site — not a blog or a coupon site — and the whole list is reviewed every week. Offers that no longer work are removed, and the check date is shown at the top of this page.

Do I need a card for free cloud storage?

No. Google Drive gives 15 GB free, pCloud 10 GB and Dropbox 2 GB — all three start with just an email, no card.

Is there a free VPN that needs no card?

Yes — Proton VPN is free forever with unlimited data and asks for no card. The NordVPN deal on this page is a discount on a paid plan, so it does need a card.

Where can I edit a PDF free online with no sign-up?

Sejda's PDF editor runs in your browser with no sign-up: files up to 200 pages or 50 MB, 3 free tasks per hour, and files are deleted after 2 hours.

Which streaming free trials need no card?

None of the trials on this page — Apple TV+, YouTube Premium and Amazon Prime all ask for a card to start. For streaming with no card, use the free tiers: YouTube, Spotify Free and SoundCloud need only an email.

Are there free online courses with a free certificate?

Yes — freeCodeCamp's coding certifications are completely free. Coursera lets you audit top-university courses free, but its certificate is paid.

Can I download free PC games legally?

Yes. The Epic Games Store gives away 1–2 full games free every week — claim one and it is yours to keep. Steam also has hundreds of free-to-play games.

Do free AI writing tools need a card?

No. The free plans of ChatGPT, Claude, Google Gemini and Microsoft Copilot start with just an email — no card.

Where can I get free stock photos with no attribution?

Canva's free plan includes stock photos you can use in your designs. Unsplash, Pexels and Pixabay also offer photos under licences that do not require attribution — they are examples, not offers listed on this page.

How to get free Zoom premium

You can't get Zoom's paid plans free as an individual. Zoom's Basic plan is free forever, but group meetings end after 40 minutes. The only real routes to a paid plan free are the Zoom for Startups program — 12 months of Business Plus free for eligible early-stage startups (Seed/Series A) — and a university-licensed account from your school or workplace. There is no student discount.

Is ChatGPT free

Yes — ChatGPT has a free plan with unlimited text chats. Plus is the paid plan at $20/month.

Is Duolingo really free

Yes — all Duolingo courses are free, with ads and Energy limits on the free plan. Super is the paid plan.
